rules.title: Base: incompressible setup — pressure-based
rules.why: For incompressible and weakly compressible flows the standard segregated pressure-based solver is used; in 3ddp it is enabled by default (07_SOLVER §1).

rules.title: Mach >= 0.3: density-based-implicit + compressibility + energy
rules.why: At Mach >= 0.3 compressibility matters: the coupled-implicit density-based solver is more robust for trans/supersonic flows and shocks; a compressible gas needs the energy equation and ideal-gas density. The 0.3 threshold is engineering practice; the KB has no explicit threshold, hence status derived.

rules.title: Mach < 0.3: stay with pressure-based
rules.why: At Mach < 0.3 compressibility can be neglected; pressure-based is simpler and cheaper, p-v-coupling Coupled (code 24) is the standard scheme.

rules.title: Pressure-velocity coupling scheme for pressure-based
rules.why: A new case defaults to 24 (Coupled); the codes are verified: 20 SIMPLE, 21 SIMPLEC, 22 PISO, 24 Coupled. For porous/complex cases the user sets 20 (SIMPLE) — a deliberate decision, not the default.

rules.title: Re < 5000: laminar model
rules.why: In the verified working journal the switching threshold is Re = 5000: below the threshold a laminar setup is used, and setup_case.jou is always laminar.

rules.title: Re >= 5000: k-omega SST
rules.why: At Re >= 5000 the flow is turbulent; the verified working journal enables k-omega SST (at runtime, from switch_to_turbulence.jou) and switches the inlet to mass-flow-inlet with 10% intensity and viscosity ratio 30.

rules.title: Heat transfer: enable the energy equation
rules.why: The energy equation unlocks thermal BCs, radiation, CHT, shell conduction, solidification; without it the temperature is not solved. The 5-question chain is verified.

rules.title: High temperatures (>= 1000 K): energy is mandatory
rules.why: At temperatures around 1000 K and above, variable properties and radiation cannot be neglected; the energy equation is a prerequisite for radiation and temperature-dependent properties.

rules.title: T >= 1000 K: Discrete Ordinates radiation
rules.why: At T >= 1000 K the radiative heat flux becomes significant; DO is the main working option for combustion/furnaces (KB 04_MODELS/radiation.md §2.2). The ~1000 K threshold is engineering practice (the KB has no explicit threshold), hence status derived.

rules.title: Compressible gas: ideal-gas density
rules.why: The ideal-gas method requires the energy equation to be enabled (Fluent enables it itself); both journal forms — fluid and mixture — are verified.

rules.title: Combustion: Species Transport with a mixture material
rules.why: For combustion, a user material database (.src) with a mixture material and a mechanism is imported first, then species-transport is enabled with the mixture name; without a mixture material the model will not turn on.

rules.title: Combustion: volumetric reactions + stiff chemistry
rules.why: The mechanism from the .src contains reactions/reaction-mechs; volumetric-reactions are enabled to get sources; for detailed mechanisms — stiff-chemistry. The lines are verified by the user journal.

rules.title: Combustion with a UDF: volume-reaction-rate hook
rules.why: The user UDF mechanism replaces the reaction rate via DEFINE_VR_RATE and the volume-reaction-rate hook "<function>::<library>"; the library must be compiled and loaded beforehand.

rules.title: Multiphase: default model selection
rules.why: If multiphase flow is needed but the type is not specified — the base choice is VOF for sharp phase interfaces; then the multiphase.vof/eulerian/mixture rules refine the model by physics.multiphase.model.

rules.title: VOF multiphase
rules.why: VOF is for sharp phase interfaces; it usually requires a transient setup. The TUI question is verified: Available options ("none" "vof" "eulerian" "mixture" "wetsteam").

rules.title: Eulerian multiphase
rules.why: Eulerian suits dense dispersed/bubbly flows with interphase interaction; it requires the number of phases and usually transient.

rules.title: Mixture multiphase
rules.why: Mixture is a simplified model for weakly coupled phases; it can be solved steady-state and is cheaper than Eulerian; used when interface details are not needed.

rules.title: Particles: DPM (discrete phase)
rules.why: DPM is activated by creating an injection; two-way coupling is enabled for particles to affect the gas. It requires a mesh; for evaporation/reactions — energy/species. The KB has no verified full chain.

rules.title: Transient setup
rules.why: For physically transient problems (rotating machinery, VOF, pulsed processes) unsteady is enabled; 2nd order is more accurate. The full /solve/set/transient-controls/* chains were not captured in the KB.

rules.title: UDF: compile → load → hook
rules.why: All user working journals use compiled UDFs only: compile the library, load it, then bind the hook. Interpreted is not used in their practice; the function-hooks menu appears after load.

rules.title: Axisymmetry: 2D-axisymmetric + axis zone type
rules.why: An axisymmetric problem needs a 2D axisymmetric setup (the dimensionality is set when starting Fluent, 2ddp) and the axis of rotation as an axis-type zone; the /define/models/axisymmetric? command is registered in the internal tree but was not observed in the live menu.

rules.title: Porous zone: fluid + porous + UDF properties
rules.why: A porous medium is set in the fluid zone (Porous zone? yes): directions, viscous/inertial resistance, porosity; for conjugate heat transfer UDF/UDM may be needed, and physical-velocity-porous-formulation for physical velocity.

rules.title: Stopping criteria: residual + conv-reports + reporting-interval
rules.why: In the working project stopping is combined: residual thresholds (5 values, the last one is energy), report-based criteria (conv-reports) and reporting-interval so that the external Scheme loop can step in. strict mode: energy 5e-6/stop 1e-3/window 1000/freq 100; relaxed mode: 5e-4/5e-3/500/50.
